text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet has agreed with the visiting International Monetary Fund mission to provide for a $65-70 average montly salary in the public sector at the year-end, Social care minister Ivan Neikov said. @
-- Iran was ready to renew deliveries of crude oil to Bulgaria and was interested in the planned privatisation of Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery Neftochim, Iranian ambassador in Bulgaria said.
Bulgaria halted imports of Iranian crude last year when Neftochim moved to processing Russian crude only. @

-- It was not true that the Turkey's Sise Cam glass maker was expected to buy a 25 percent stake from the 60-percent equity of the Belgian Solvay SA in the Bulgarian soda ash producer Sodi Devnya because such a transfer was not provided for in Solvay's contract with Bulgaria, Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev.
-- Bulgaria's prosecutor-general launched an investigation into former Agriculture minister Vassil Chichibaba and three of his deputies on possible criminal negligence charges over grain exports. @

-- Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet temporarily cancelled licences of non-ferous metals scrap traders in a bid to fight widespread thefts of energy and communication cables, Interior minister Bogomil Bonev said.

-- Bulgaria's interim cabinet would sell wheat deliveries from Poland at $150 per tonne to local grain mills, Agriculture minister Roumen Hristov said. The cabinet expected bread price to rise by some 60 levs per kilo at most at that price of wheat. @
-- Central heating charges are expected to rise 3.5 times to the equivalent of $20 from April under a proposal by the Energy ministry if Bulgaria's caretaker cabinet approves it.
-- Bulgaria's central bank refinancing to commercial banks totalled 55.874 billion levs at the end of February of which 54.83 billion levs were overdue loans and deposits.

-- Bulgaria's central government budget deficit rose by 24.3 billion levs in the second half of February to 222.1 billion levs, Finance Ministry figures showed. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
